item.title: Between 60 to 102 Malden road, 15th November
item.description:
Dear Camden Council Highways Team, I am writing to formally report the deteriorating road surface on Malden Road, particularly near 82C Malden Road. Sections of the road appear to be subsiding, creating deep dips that cause buses and heavy vehicles to bounce as they pass. The resulting vibrations shake nearby properties and may be contributing to cracks and structural damage. As shown on the attached annotated map: - Green: Sections previously resurfaced by Camden Council. - Red: Sections experiencing apparent subsidence that require urgent attention. We request an urgent highways inspection and appropriate remedial works to address the subsidence and prevent further damage. We would welcome Council engineers to inspect our property and witness firsthand the significant vibrations caused by passing buses and heavy vehicles. Please treat this letter as formal notice of the potential damage to surrounding properties. We reserve the right to hold Camden Council liable for any damage attributable to the road's condition, particularly if appropriate action is not taken following this notification. Please acknowledge receipt, provide a case reference number and confirm the proposed action and timescale. Kind regards, Resident 82C Malden Road London Attachment: Annotated map of Malden Road showing previously resurfaced sections (green) and areas of apparent subsidence (red).

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 106, Malden Road, Kentish Town, Greater London

item.title: Request for bench removal due to antisocial behaviour & drug use (not a cleaning request), 15th November
item.description:
Please forward this to the Community Safety / ASB team and Highways management. This newly installed bench on the corner of Elcot and Friary rd which we are greatful for is attracting persistent open drug use and loitering, leading to increased security concerns. There have been at least 2 attempted break-ins at neighbors on friary road in the last month. We are requesting its permanent removal, as I hear the council has previously done with another bench in the area for the exact same reasons.
